gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured real-world output for small wind turbines. In the Warwick Wind Trials, 26 UK turbines rated 400–1,500 W averaged 78 kWh a year each, or 8.9 W, which is 0.85% of their rating. That 8.9 W is about the same as the idle draw The Solar Lab measured on the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (9.5 W).
standout_why: I compared against these pages. Our own Dealectric page (cited) has no tested figures; its wind numbers are the maker's 150 W at 27 mph plus a cube-law estimate of 'a few watts' at 10 mph. The Nature's Generator L3600 and L6000 store pages (cited) are spec sheets. I could not open them directly because the site returned a self-signed certificate error, but the search results show only maker ratings: 150 W at 27 mph, about 13 mph start-up on the 350 W unit. The DOE Small Wind Guidebook (cited) is siting guidance and its URL now redirects. The solargenerator.guide review states it reports no measured figures and uses rated Wh × 0.85 as an estimate. None of these gives a measured turbine yield from a named trial, and none gives measured capacity, efficiency or idle draw for any candidate station.
decides: It supports the current wording, which already plays wind down: the L3600 stays the pick only for a shopper who must have a wind port and has a strong, open site. The measured trials show a typical small turbine averages single-digit to tens of watts, so for most buyers the wind port adds little. That favors stations whose measured efficiency and idle draw are good. Here only the Elite 200 V2 has a full set: APH Networks drained 2,028 Wh of 2,073.6 Wh (97.8%), and The Solar Lab measured 94% efficiency and 9.5 W idle. No independent test exists for the L3600, L6000 or MyGrid 10K, so the wind pick rests on maker specs alone. The page should say so.

findings.label: Warwick Wind Trials: average output of 26 building-mounted small turbines (rated 400–1,500 W)
findings.value: 78 kWh/year per turbine = 8.9 W average (0.85% of rated); 230 kWh/year = 26 W (4.15%) excluding downtime
findings.source_title: Real-world tests of small wind turbines in Netherlands and the UK (Kris De Decker, Resilience.org)
findings.note: Encraft's Warwick Wind Trials Project, 26 UK sites, October 2007 to October 2008, published January 2009. Models: Ampair 600, Eclectic StealthGen, Zephyr Air Dolphin Z1000, Windsave WS1000/WS1200, Swift. All were building-mounted, which is worse than a pole 30 ft above obstructions. The control electronics used an average of 29 kWh/year per turbine. The primary PDF (s1.solacity.com mirror) would not extract, so these figures come via De Decker.

findings.label: Warwick Wind Trials: best and worst site
findings.value: Best 2.382 kWh/day while operating (≈869 kWh/yr, ≈99 W avg); worst 41 Wh/day (≈15 kWh/yr, ≈1.7 W), less than its own electronics consumed
findings.source_title: Warwick Wind Trials Gives Failing Grade to Rooftop Wind (Paul Gipe, wind-works.org, 2009-07-16)
findings.note: The best site was on a high-rise building. Gipe quotes the Encraft final report. The average watt figures are my conversions (kWh/yr ÷ 8,760 h). De Decker gives the same 869 and 15 kWh/yr.

findings.label: Dutch Zeeland small-turbine field test: measured annual yield
findings.value: 73–578 kWh/yr (8.3–66 W average) for seven small models (Energy Ball v100, Ampair 600, Turby, Airdolphin, WRE 030/060, Passaat); Skystream 2,109 kWh/yr (240.7 W); Montana 2,691 kWh/yr (307 W)
findings.source_title: Real-world tests of small wind turbines in Netherlands and the UK (Kris De Decker, Resilience.org)
findings.note: 12 turbines in a row on an open plain, 2008-04-01 to 2009-03-31; 3 broke. The site averaged 3.8 m/s (≈8.5 mph), which a station 14 km away disputed (6 m/s); the organizers called the figure 'only indicative'.

findings.label: Drain test, usable AC energy
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review (Page 4 of 5), APH Networks
findings.note: 987 W electric heater ran 2 h 1 min until shutoff. The screen read 1,006 W for the 987 W load. The page gives no review date.

findings.label: Idle draw and efficiency
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 Review, The Solar Lab
findings.note: The page prints '9.5W per hour'; the unit should be W. It calls the 94% the highest it has measured on a power station. The reviewers' panels peaked at 800 W of the 1,000 W solar rating. No byline or date on the page.

findings.label: Discharge and recharge energy
findings.value: 1.91 kWh out; 2.44 kWh in to refill (≈78% round trip)
findings.source_title: Portable Power Meets Lab-Grade Reliability: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review, StorageReview (Dylan Dougherty, 2025-04-25)
findings.note: The round-trip figure is my arithmetic: 1.91 ÷ 2.44. The review does not describe its method. Its UPS test with servers drew 986 W to 1.1 kW. The result is well below APH's 2,028 Wh.

findings.label: High-draw test, usable energy
findings.source_title: Bluetti Apex 300: The Latest Entry in the Stackable Power Station Wars, Outdoor Life (Laura Lancaster, 2025-05-20)
findings.note: Dehumidifier load, measured with a Kill-a-Watt meter. In the same test the Anker SOLIX C1000 gave 950 Wh (90%) and the Jackery Explorer 1000 Plus 1,090 Wh (86%). Measured AC recharge was about 2 h.

findings.label: Idle draw and efficiency
findings.source_title: Bluetti Apex 300 review, The Solar Lab
findings.note: The reviewer says a full unit would idle itself empty in about 6 days. Efficiency comes from a mix of loads on the AC outlets. No byline or date on the page.

findings.label: Measured wall-charging power
findings.value: 508 W silent; 1,442 W auto; 2,330 W peak turbo
findings.source_title: Bluetti APEX 300 battery storage system review, Notebookcheck (Christian Hintze, 2025-08-10)
findings.note: Notebookcheck did not measure usable capacity, efficiency or idle draw. Weather kept them from testing maximum solar input.

unsourced: Nature's Generator L3600, L6000 and MyGrid 10K Gen 2: independent measured usable Wh, efficiency, idle draw or charge time. I checked solargenerator.guide (it uses a 0.85 multiplier and says it has no tests), searched for YouTube and hands-on Kill-a-Watt tests, and checked the brand blog (promotional only). None found.

Nature's Generator 150 W and 350 W turbines: measured output at any wind speed from a reviewer or lab. Only the maker's 150 W at 27 mph, 350 W at 27 mph and ≈13 mph start-up turned up, and Home Depot owner reviews have no numbers. The maker's pages returned a self-signed certificate error to WebFetch and the storecheck tool, so I could not reread the rival pages either.
Warwick Wind Trials primary report (s1.solacity.com mirror): the PDF text would not extract, so its figures come via Kris De Decker (Resilience.org) and Paul Gipe (wind-works.org).
DOE Small Wind Guidebook (cited by ChatGPT): the windexchange.energy.gov PDF now redirects to the WINDExchange home page, so I could not confirm its figures.
An urban 400 W turbine study on ResearchGate (≈85 W peak, 10–15 Wh/day): seen only in a search summary and not opened, so left out.
